task.request: Assess the supplied item handlers against the accepted changed policy and request a source change that permits only an item's authenticated owner to read or modify it, with no active-superuser exception.

policySources.text: Only the authenticated owner may read or modify an existing item; active superuser status alone grants no exception for an item owned by someone else.

acceptance.reason: This is the task author's fixed changed policy and must be assessed independently of the unchanged implementation behavior.

principals.description: Author facts: ["current_user is authenticated and active","current_user.is_superuser is false"]
startingCapabilities: May read or modify only items owned by current_user under the accepted policy

principals.description: Author facts: ["current_user is authenticated and active","current_user.is_superuser is true"]
startingCapabilities: May read or modify only items owned by current_user under the accepted policy

resources.description: Author facts: ["The item exists at handler entry","The item's owner_id differs from current_user.id in both scenarios"]

obligations.relation: item is owned by another user
item is owned by another user

task.scopeAssurance: Only explicitly declared scenarios and supplied source are assessed; repository discovery and deployment behavior are not tested.
requiredAnalysis: Trace entry, identity and resource binding, strongest authorization control, and protected effect. Explain decisive missing source-external facts.
constraints: Use only supplied fixed source context. Do not execute or modify the target, contact a deployment, or claim repository-wide discovery.

analysisRequirements.question: Which source-visible condition or control gates the declared entry before the assessed path proceeds?
How is the declared principal bound to the runtime caller or identity used by the assessed operation?
How is the request-selected object bound to the declared resource, and which other checked resource must remain distinct?
What is the strongest source-visible authorization decision for this principal, resource relation, operation, and condition set, including any role or ownership branch?
After the visible controls, can the requested operation reach the declared protected effect, and under which source-visible branch?
Which source-external fact, if any, can change the answer, and is that fact supplied or still unknown in this fixed context?

analysisContract.publicInstruction: Use only the supplied items.py source crop. The analysis boundary is each declared handler entry, and the stated identity, activity, existence, and ownership facts are task premises at that entry rather than proof of upstream injection or deployment behavior. Assess only the two supplied scenarios against the accepted changed policy, do not pretend the source changed, and identify the required owner-only source change without consulting an evaluator.

premises.statement: At update_item handler entry, current_user is the stated active non-superuser and the existing item's owner differs from current_user.id.

requiredResponseDetails: State the changed-policy judgment for changing the foreign-owned existing item.
Explain whether the supplied update handler enforces that judgment.
Request any change needed to enforce owner-only modification without a superuser exception.

premises.statement: At read_item handler entry, current_user is the stated authenticated active superuser and the existing item's owner differs from current_user.id.

requiredResponseDetails: State the changed-policy judgment for reading the foreign-owned existing item.
Explain whether the supplied read handler enforces that judgment.
Request removal of any active-superuser ownership bypass needed to enforce owner-only reading.
